description: Three-panel composite figure combining EBSD maps with an XRD pattern, all from the initial as-forged steel. (a) EBSD inverse pole figure (IPF) map: a fully indexed, equiaxed grain structure with grains spanning roughly 10-50 µm, each grain coloured according to its crystallographic orientation (red, blue, green, magenta, yellow domains), an inset orientation colour triangle key marked 001 (top), 101 (left), 111 (right), and a 50 µm scale bar at bottom right; black grain boundaries are drawn. (b) EBSD phase map of the same field: the whole mapped area is uniformly red with black grain-boundary lines and no second-phase regions, i.e. a single indexed phase, with a matching 50 µm scale bar. (c) XRD patterns plotted as Intensity (a.u.) versus 2θ = 40-90°, two vertically offset curves labelled by a legend: black "Initial" (lower) and red "-196 °C" (upper); both show only four reflections, annotated γ(111) (near 43°), γ(200) (near 50°), γ(220) (near 74°) and γ(311) (near 90°), with no extra peaks. Taken together the panels argue that the starting microstructure is single-phase austenite and that holding at −196 °C for 30 min produces no isothermal martensite, i.e. the austenite is very stable. No numeric peak positions or intensities are printed.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an EBSD IPF map with a 50 µm scale bar showing equiaxed grains of roughly 10-50 µm, each grain coloured by crystallographic orientation.
The IPF colour key inset in (a) is marked 001 at the top (red), 101 at the left (blue) and 111 at the right (green).
Panel (b) is a phase map that is uniformly red over the whole field, separated only by black grain-boundary lines, indicating a single indexed phase with no second-phase regions.
Panel (c) plots Intensity (a.u.) against 2θ over 40-90° for two conditions displayed as vertically offset curves, a black 'Initial' curve below and a red '-196 °C' curve above.
Both XRD curves in (c) contain only four labelled reflections - γ(111) near 43°, γ(200) near 50°, γ(220) near 74° and γ(311) near 90° - with no additional peaks of any other phase.

The caption identifies panel (a) as the EBSD IPF map and (b) as the phase map of the initial steel, and (c) as the XRD pattern of the initial steel and of the steel after holding at −196 °C for 30 min.
The citing text states that the initial microstructure consists of equiaxed grains with a fully austenitic constituent.
The citing text states that the XRD patterns of the as-forged and the −196 °C-treated steel show that no isothermal martensite forms at −196 °C and that the austenite is very stable.
The citing text reports an estimated density of 7.078 g/cm³ and a measured density of 7.114 g/cm³ for the steel, a value that is not shown in any panel of this figure.
Grain-boundary misorientation character (e.g. low- vs high-angle) and phase-fraction values are not printed anywhere in this figure.

subfigures.description: EBSD IPF map of the initial as-forged steel: equiaxed grains of varied orientation colours (red/blue/green/magenta) with black grain boundaries, an inset colour key triangle labelled 001 (top), 101 (left), 111 (right), and a 50 µm scale bar at bottom right; the '(a)' label sits at top left.

EBSD phase map of the same field, rendered almost entirely in red with black grain-boundary lines outlining equiaxed grains and a few small dotted/red artifacts; no second-phase colour appears. 50 µm scale bar at bottom right, '(b)' label at top left. No on-image legend identifies the red phase.

XRD patterns with Intensity (a.u.) on the y-axis and 2θ (°) on the x-axis from 40 to 90, two offset curves: black 'Initial' below and red '-196 °C' above. Both contain only four labelled reflections - γ(111), γ(200), γ(220), γ(311); no other peaks are present.
